title: Fresh install is met by a wall, not a room
observation: The first real screen after a blank splash is a full-screen gate: "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love", then "Sign in with Apple", "Continue with Google", "Continue with email", a divider reading "or", and only then "Look around first →", with "Have a password? Sign in" beneath it.
why_it_matters: A skeptical buyer decides in three seconds whether an app is for him or for its own funnel, and the door he wants is the fourth option under a divider.
already_ruled: C9 (auth = Supabase, passwordless-first + soft wall, guests browse) — the soft wall is ruled; the gate-first-screen ordering is shipped behaviour, not ruled copy
proposal_seed: Promote "Look around first" above the divider as the primary act on first launch.

title: Three icon systems in three stacked buttons
observation: "Sign in with Apple" carries Apple's real logo; "Continue with Google" carries a bare typed letter "G"; "Continue with email" carries a stock colour emoji envelope — three different icon systems in three adjacent buttons.
why_it_matters: The first screen of a company selling craft argues, visually, that nobody proofread it — which is exactly the doubt a $4,000 purchase cannot survive.
proposal_seed: Replace the emoji and the typed G with monochrome SF Symbols matching the app's own weight.

title: Launch screen is blank white, no wordmark
observation: The launch screen is pure blank white — no wordmark, no strata mark, no colour — before the warm cream ground of the app appears. Captured identically on two separate cold launches.
why_it_matters: The one moment the brand owns unconditionally is spent on nothing, and the white flash reads as a broken load.
proposal_seed: Put the cream ground and the PATINA wordmark on the launch storyboard so the splash and the app agree.

title: Tour's middle step never renders
observation: The tour presents "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" and "Step 2 of 2 / Your profile". The declared middle step — "Save what you love" / "Add pieces to a room with + Add — they follow you everywhere." — never appears, because its anchor `.addToRoom` mounts in no view and the model drops it after a 1.5s grace.
why_it_matters: The one first-run sentence that explains the app's save-and-return loop is silently omitted, and it names a "+ Add" control that does not exist on the shipped home.
already_ruled: C18 (tour content is canonical and delivered) — the copy is ruled; the dropped anchor is a named residual, not a re-proposal
july_status: U32 DELIVERED-VERIFIED — residual: the anchor was on the now-orphaned DailyProductCard
proposal_seed: Anchor step 2 to the Active Room card and rewrite it for the save path that actually ships.

title: Coach marks cover the cards they explain
observation: The "Step 1 of 2 / Welcome to Patina" bubble sits directly on top of the Next Move card it is describing, with "Skip" and "Next" rendered in iOS system blue #007AFF — the only blue in an otherwise brown and cream app. Step 2 covers the same card again, and the Companion intro card follows immediately.
why_it_matters: Three consecutive overlays that hide their own subject teach a first-time user that the app talks over itself.
proposal_seed: Offset each bubble below its anchor and tint the tour controls with the app's clay, not system blue.

title: Only the date changes between two mornings
observation: The home is four blocks: "WEDNESDAY · AUG 26" + "Today", one "NEXT MOVE" card, one story card, one "ACTIVE ROOM" card. Across guest, engaged, activeProject, dark mode and a relaunch, the only element guaranteed to differ from yesterday is the date string.
why_it_matters: A daily-return product whose sole honest daily change is a date has no reason to be opened daily.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B's Today contract: exactly one next move, one real story, one active room) — the contract is accepted; the finding is that none of the three is time-keyed
proposal_seed: Add one dated, event-sourced line above the Next Move card naming what changed since the last open.

title: Story's unread dot is permanently on
observation: The clay unread dot on the "MAKER SPOTLIGHT / The Grain Whisperer of Maine" card is drawn on every capture in every lane and every tier, because `isUnread` is hard-coded `true` in the client.
why_it_matters: A freshness signal that is always on is a lie the reader eventually catches, and it costs the app every other honest signal on the screen.
already_ruled: C5 (honesty: no fabricated signals), C28 (already named as an honesty candidate)
proposal_seed: Persist a read timestamp per story id and drive the dot from it.

title: One story, forever, out of three that exist
observation: "MAKER SPOTLIGHT / The Grain Whisperer of Maine / Jonathan Chilton on 40 years of listening to wood" is the same card on the guest home, the engaged home, the activeProject home, in dark mode and after a relaunch. The fetch is `order=sort_order.desc,published_at.desc&limit=1` with no per-day or per-user selection, and the catalogue holds three stories.
why_it_matters: The single piece of content a maker-story reader would return for is the one thing on the screen that provably cannot be new tomorrow.
already_ruled: C3 (editorial feel of the Daily Room is ruled) — this asks for cadence, not a different module
proposal_seed: Serve the newest unread story per user, dated, and commission enough of them to make a weekly cadence honest.

title: Says "Today" but never reads the hour
observation: The header reads "WEDNESDAY · AUG 26" over the literal word "Today". `TimeOfDay` exists with dawn/morning/day/afternoon/evening/night boundaries but is read only by the camera primer and two Companion greeting generators — never by the home.
why_it_matters: A 7:40am screen and a 9:10pm screen are identical, so the app can never feel like it was made for the moment it is being opened in.
proposal_seed: Read TimeOfDay in the greeting header and let morning, evening and night pick different one-line copy.

title: No search anywhere in the app
observation: There is no search field on the home, on "Browse pieces", in Saved, or anywhere else; the only narrowing controls are five hard-coded chips — "All", "Seating", "Tables", "Lighting", "Storage" — which filter the twenty rows already fetched and never send a category to the server.
why_it_matters: A buyer who already knows what he wants — a reading chair, a walnut sideboard — has no way to say so, and browsing ten curated tiles is not a substitute.
proposal_seed: Add one search field over the catalogue and pass the query and category server-side.

title: Browse grid runs off the left edge
observation: The two-column grid places cards at x = −32.7 and x = −10.7 and ends one at x = 412.7 on a 402pt screen, at four different sizes (284×294, 171×341, 240×293, 240×304). The left column reads "M & BOARD", "rloom Oak / ing Table", ",200". Under "Seating" the cards overlap and one renders as a blank brown gradient with no image.
why_it_matters: The app's only commerce surface cannot show a maker's name or a price without cutting them in half, in light, in dark and at large type.
proposal_seed: Replace the hand-sized cards with a fixed-metric LazyVGrid and pin one card size per column.

title: Dimensions and lead time exist nowhere
observation: The piece surface carries maker, name, materials as a joined subtitle, price, an "{n}% match" pill, provenance chips and a maker story. It carries no dimensions, no lead time, no stock, no shipping, no returns policy, no description and no link to the maker's own page. `products.dimensions JSONB` exists in the schema and is neither returned by `get_recommendations` nor decoded by the app.
why_it_matters: Nobody buys a four-thousand-dollar chair without knowing whether it fits through the door or when it arrives; two of the five fields a purchase needs are in the database and simply never sent.
proposal_seed: Widen `get_recommendations` and the product fetch to return dimensions and lead_time_weeks, and render them under the price.

title: Photographs do not match the pieces
observation: "Heirloom Oak Dining Table" (Room & Board) is illustrated with a white table ringed by green velvet chairs; "Live-Edge Coffee Table" (Lee Industries) is illustrated with an old ladder-back chair standing on grass; the same green-velvet image reappears as the saved item's thumbnail.
why_it_matters: On a marketplace whose argument is provenance, a picture that is not the object destroys the only evidence a remote buyer has.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B contract: "the app does not invent or mislabel imagery")
proposal_seed: Gate a product out of the feed unless its image row belongs to that product.

title: "UNKNOWN MAKER" on a provenance marketplace
observation: Two of the ten curated cards print the maker line as "UNKNOWN MAKER" where others read "ROOM & BOARD", "LEE INDUSTRIES", "HOLLY HUNT", "MITCHELL GOLD + BOB WILLIAMS".
why_it_matters: The maker is the reason to buy here rather than anywhere else; an unnamed one is a piece with no story and no recourse.
already_ruled: C5 (honesty), C6 (designers/makers are the intelligence layer)
proposal_seed: Exclude products with no resolvable vendor from the curated feed rather than labelling them unknown.

title: "46% match" names nothing it matches
observation: Cards carry "46% match", "45% match", "43% match", "41% match"; Profile shows "48% MATCH" then "63% MATCH" after signing in; the room shows "— MATCH". Nothing on any of those screens states what is being matched against or why the number moved.
why_it_matters: A number about me that I cannot interrogate is worse than no number — it invites the suspicion that it is decorative.
already_ruled: U02/U43 — the fabricated-number half is closed; this is the unexplained-label half
july_status: U02 DELIVERED-VERIFIED (real varying scores), U43 DELIVERED-VERIFIED (qualitative copy) — residual is the bare percentage on the card
proposal_seed: Replace the bare percentage with the rationale line the app already computes, or make the pill tappable to explain itself.

title: Every piece detail fails and traps the user
observation: Every product tap in every lane returns "Couldn't load product" / "Let's try that again". Retry fails identically, the edge-swipe back does nothing, and `scan_ui` returns exactly one element for the whole screen — the retry link. The only escape is force-quitting the app. Root cause: `GET /rest/v1/products?id=eq.…&select=*,vendors(name,made_in,brand_story)` returns HTTP 300 `PGRST201`, because `products` carries two foreign keys to `vendors`.
why_it_matters: The screen where a buyer reads the maker's story and the price is unreachable, and reaching for it destroys a guest's whole session.
already_ruled: C27 names this explicitly as app-side and fair game (distinct from the local edge-function 503s)
proposal_seed: Disambiguate the embed to `vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey(...)` and give the error state a Back control.

title: Saved has no door until something is saved
observation: The Companion's "Saved" row returns nil when `context.tableItemCount == 0`, and that count sums room `SavedItem`s — not the `TableItemModel` rows a heart on the browse grid or the piece detail writes. `scan_ui` on the panel confirmed no "Saved" row at either 0-room or 1-room state.
why_it_matters: A user who saves the way the app invites him to save can end up with a Saved screen that has no entry point anywhere in the application, so the investment he made is invisible on return.
already_ruled: C1 (Companion + hub rail are the nav) — this is the row's own gate, not a tab-bar proposal
july_status: U09/U24 DELIVERED — the MarketplaceLinksSection that carried the permanent Saved door is now orphaned (C23)
proposal_seed: Count TableItemModel rows in tableItemCount and show the Saved row unconditionally.

title: Saved opens on boards that can never fill
observation: Saved's default tab is "Boards", reading "No boards yet" / "Save pieces from recommendations to create your first board" / "Create Board" — while the Companion simultaneously reports "1 SAVED PIECE". A created board reads "This board is empty" permanently, because `CollectionsViewModel.addToBoard(_:productId:)` has no call site anywhere in the app.
why_it_matters: The default view of the only place investment accumulates is empty by construction, so the app's memory of what I love looks like nothing.
already_ruled: C28 (already named: boards can be created but never hold a piece)
proposal_seed: Default the tab to "All items" until a board exists, and wire addToBoard to the ⋯ menu.

title: Saved prints "$4200" without a comma
observation: The saved row reads "ROOM & BOARD / Heirloom Oak Dining Table / $4200" while the same piece on the browse grid reads "$4,200".
why_it_matters: Money formatted two ways on two screens of the same app is the smallest possible tell that nobody owns the numbers.
proposal_seed: Route every price through the one currency formatter the grid already uses.

title: Re-saving a piece inserts a duplicate
observation: The piece detail's primary button reads "Add to Room" and becomes "Saved ✓", but `isSaved` is never seeded from storage on entry, and the standard `.pieceDetail(pieceId:)` route passes no room context — so a piece saved yesterday shows "Add to Room" again today and a second `TableItemModel` row is inserted.
why_it_matters: The app forgets an investment the user made and then quietly doubles it, which is the opposite of the memory a return product is selling.
already_ruled: C28 (named: re-saving duplicates rows)
proposal_seed: Seed isSaved from the local store on appear and make toggleSave idempotent on productId.

title: 18 × 14 ft is stored as 59' × 46'
observation: With the toggle reading "ft", LENGTH 18 and WIDTH 14 were typed; the next screen — "YOUR SPACE / Here's what I see." — returned a room of "46 ft" × "59 ft" and "2713 SQUARE FEET", and those figures persist into the room view ("Living Room / 2713 SQ FT · 2 WINDOWS", "59' × 46'"), Your Spaces, and the home's ACTIVE ROOM card.
why_it_matters: The app silently multiplies the one measurement a downsizer cares about by 3.28 and then presents it back as fact — after which no number it shows can be believed.
proposal_seed: Apply the metre-to-foot conversion only when the unit toggle is actually on "m", and echo the entered unit on the summary.

title: Unit toggle is a 6-point silent target
observation: The "ft / m" control in the ROOM DIMENSIONS header exposes "ft" at 12×13pt and "m" at 6×13pt. Tapping "m" produced no visible state change — "ft" stayed bold — while silently changing how the typed numbers were interpreted. Steppers are 32×32.
why_it_matters: A six-point target with no visible state is how a sixty-three-year-old's room gets recorded at four times its size without him ever seeing a control change.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B trust contract: controls at least 44×44 points)
proposal_seed: Make ft/m a 44pt segmented control with an unmistakable selected state.

title: A typed form calls itself a scan
observation: The Next Move promises "A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from." and opens a typed form. The summary then offers "Rescan" and reports "0 ITEMS DETECTED" for a room nobody scanned; Your Spaces stamps the room "JUST SCANNED" directly above its own caption "2713 SQ FT · MANUAL ENTRY"; the Studio lists it as "Living Room / SCANNED AUG 26".
why_it_matters: Four surfaces claim a capture that never happened, which is the fastest way to make a buyer distrust everything else the app claims to know about his house.
already_ruled: C12 (manual entry is the ruled non-LiDAR fallback) — the fallback is ruled, the scan vocabulary on it is not
proposal_seed: Give the manual path its own vocabulary — "Edit details", "Entered by you" — and drop the scan chips and detection counts.

title: No way to put a piece into a room
observation: The card ⋯ menu offers only "Save", "Share", "Not for me", "View details" — no "Add to room" — including when the grid is entered from the room's own "Browse Picks for This Room" button, which opens the same unfiltered "10 pieces curated for your space" with no room name. The room meanwhile reads "A blank canvas" / "We've already found pieces that would fit this space. Browse your Daily Room to start building this room." and counts "0 ITEMS".
why_it_matters: The room is meant to be the thing worth returning to, and the app makes it impossible to put anything in it.
already_ruled: C28 (AddToRoomSheet/AddedToRoomToast exist with no presenter)
proposal_seed: Mount AddToRoomSheet on the card menu and pass the room's remoteId through the room-scoped browse.

title: "0 IN AR" counts a feature that cannot exist
observation: The room stat row reads "0 ITEMS", "— MATCH", "0 IN AR", with "IN AR" undefined on screen. `usdz_url` is `NULL::text` in the recommendations RPC and hard-coded nil in the direct product fetch, so `hasARModel` is false on every code path: the AR button never draws, and the two remaining doors land on "3D model not available for this product".
why_it_matters: The app advertises a placement feature it structurally cannot deliver, on the screen that is supposed to prove it knows the room.
already_ruled: C28 (usdz_url always NULL so AR never renders)
proposal_seed: Hide the AR stat and the AR doors until a product actually carries a model. What would settle this: a device pass with ARKit available on a product row seeded with a real usdz_url — the Simulator cannot run ARKit, so only the null-column half is proven here.

title: Nothing on a piece helps you decide
observation: The full apparatus for deciding on a piece is the card menu — "Save", "Share", "Not for me", "View details". There is no compare surface anywhere in the app; `TableItemModel.notes` exists and no UI writes it; and the piece screen carries no "Get design help" control, though that CTA appears on eleven other surfaces.
why_it_matters: Deciding between two chairs is the actual job, and the app helps with none of it — least of all with asking a human about the thing you are looking at.
proposal_seed: Put "Ask your designer about this piece" on the piece screen, carrying the product id into the message.

title: Buying ends at "Add to Room / Saved ✓"
observation: The terminus of every browse path is a single primary button labelled "Add to Room", which becomes "Saved ✓", with only a back chevron, "?", Share and ♥ above it. There is no cart, no checkout, no "Buy", no "Request a quote", no vendor link and no `source_url` anywhere in the app; the only Stripe rail belongs to designer invoices. On the backend `direct_orders`, `create_direct_order` and the `direct_order_id` checkout branch are fully built and have zero iOS callers.
why_it_matters: There is no number of taps to money because there is no path to money, so every piece a buyer falls in love with is a referral to somebody else's checkout.
already_ruled: C11 (direct orders are a ratified backlog item, not yet designed), C24 (backend exists, no iOS client, no designer attribution)
proposal_seed: Ship a Buy path on `create_direct_order` + the existing hosted Checkout, and decide designer attribution before the button exists.

title: Sharing a chair sends the designer portal
observation: Sharing a piece from the client app opens an iOS sheet titled "Patina Designer Portal" / "app.patina.cloud". All three share sites use the same URL shape, `https://app.patina.cloud/library/<productId>`.
why_it_matters: A homeowner showing his wife a chair hands her a link branded as the professional's tool, under the professional's domain — which is both confusing and off-brand for the person who is actually buying.
proposal_seed: Point shares at a homeowner-facing patina.cloud piece page with the maker's story and Open Graph metadata.

title: The shared link cannot open the app
observation: The app declares no `com.apple.developer.associated-domains` entitlement — the entitlements file carries only `aps-environment` and `com.apple.developer.applesignin` — and `Info.plist` declares only the custom scheme `patina`. The shared `https://app.patina.cloud/library/<id>` link therefore opens Safari even for a recipient who has the app installed.
why_it_matters: Every share is a leak out of the product rather than an invitation into it, so the household's second decision-maker never lands anywhere the app can hold them.
already_ruled: C28 (no associated domains named as a standing gap)
proposal_seed: Add associated domains for patina.cloud and route `/library/<id>` to the piece detail.

title: No partner, household or second seat
observation: There is no way to share a room, a board or the Saved list — the three ShareLink sites are all single-product links. There is no invite flow, no household model, no co-viewer and no second-seat concept anywhere in the app, and no household or family-member table exists across all 487 migrations.
why_it_matters: Furniture is bought by households, not people; a product that can only hold one of a couple will be abandoned by the one it excludes.
proposal_seed: Add a single "invite your partner" seat scoped to rooms, saved items and project read access.

title: No order object; "where is it" is a bill
observation: There is no order, shipment, tracking number or delivery date anywhere in the client app. `direct_orders` carries only `pending_payment / paid / canceled` (+ refunded) with no fulfilment states, and the shipping vocabulary that does exist — confirmed, in_production, shipped, delivered, eta_change, substitution — lives on the designer-sourced `fulfillment_orders` rail and only fires when an admin operator presses send.
why_it_matters: "Where is my dining table" is the single most repeated question in a furnishing project, and the app can only answer it with an invoice.
already_ruled: C24 (direct_orders status vocabulary is only pending_payment/paid/canceled)
proposal_seed: Surface the fulfillment_orders states the backend already models as a per-piece status line in the Studio.

title: The whole Studio hides behind a 36pt monogram
observation: On the signed-in home the only chrome is a bell, a "?" and an unlabelled gold circle with the initial "C", all in the top-right corner. Everything the client owns — projects, proposals, invoices, budget, decisions, archive — is reached only by tapping that circle and scrolling past the avatar and stats to the STUDIO block. The home itself returns four content elements and no Studio row at any tier.
why_it_matters: The one screen genuinely worth returning to is behind an unlabelled 36-point target in the hardest corner to reach one-handed.
already_ruled: C1 (no tab bar), C23 (Option B's Today = four modules; the orphaned StudioHubSection is one mount away) — flagged as the open C2-vs-C23 conflict, not a tab-bar proposal
proposal_seed: Mount one "Awaiting you" summary row on Today linking into the Studio hub.

title: Three totals for one inbox, two on one screen
observation: The Studio screen prints "4 things need your eye" as its subhead and "4 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE" in the footer, directly above a block headed "Awaiting you  3"; the home and the Companion both say "2 PROJECT DECISIONS WAITING".
why_it_matters: Three different answers to "how much do I owe you" on one product is the exact arithmetic that makes a careful person stop trusting a money screen.
proposal_seed: Compute one attention count in StudioQueueBuilder and read it from the home, the Companion and the footer.

title: Deadlines vanish on the screen you act on
observation: "Due Sep 1, 2026" appears on the invoices list and on the Studio row, and nowhere on the invoice detail. "Expires Sep 8" appears on the proposals list and nowhere on the proposal detail. "Overdue · Aug 22" appears on the Studio hub and nowhere on the decisions list.
why_it_matters: Every deadline is printed on the card you leave and dropped from the page where you commit money — the one place a buyer needs to see it.
proposal_seed: Render the due/expiry date in the header of every money detail screen.

title: The engaged home is the guest home
observation: For an account whose design-request lead was accepted and claimed on Aug 18, and which already uploaded a room scan, the home reads "NEXT MOVE / Bring your first room into Patina / A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from." The Companion panel has no "Your studio" row at all, the Studio shows five zeroes — "In progress 0 / No active projects yet.", "Conversation 0", "Money & documents 0 / No shared records yet.", "Archive 0" — under the heading "Nothing needs your attention right now.", and the two-step first-launch tour re-fires.
why_it_matters: The single true fact about this account — a professional accepted them eight days ago — appears nowhere, so the moment of highest intent produces the emptiest screen.
already_ruled: C2/C23 (tier morphing is ruled; the Today ladder shipped without the engaged branch reaching this account)
proposal_seed: Make an accepted lead the Next Move — "You're matched with {designer}" — and unlock the studio row at engaged.

title: Design help offers a second request, not status
observation: "Your design request" opens on "No scans on this phone yet" / "You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below." with a single button, "Request without a scan" — for an account whose request has already been accepted. The sheet offers scanning while carrying no scan affordance.
why_it_matters: A homeowner waiting on a designer is invited to file a duplicate request instead of being told where the first one stands.
proposal_seed: Open the sheet on the existing request's stage card when a non-terminal request exists.

title: Guest hits an escape-less wall at the last tap
observation: A guest completes the whole request — "What kind of help?", "Budget (optional)", "Timeline", "Your vision (optional)", then "Review", then "Send request" — and only then is thrown the generic gate as a sheet: "Welcome home" / "Start with a piece you love", with no Cancel, no ✕ and no "Look around first". Nothing earlier in the flow says an account will be required. Only a blind downward drag dismisses it; the draft does survive.
why_it_matters: Asking for an account at the last possible tap, in copy that never mentions the request, converts effort into resentment.
already_ruled: C9 (auth sheet presents over context and never ejects) — the ejection half holds; the missing dismiss and generic copy do not
july_status: U21 DELIVERED-VERIFIED for the Notifications entry point; this is the design-request variant, unwalked in July
proposal_seed: Say "we'll need an account to send this" at the Review step, and give the sheet a Cancel.

title: "Nothing yet" while three things are due
observation: The bell opens on "Notifications / Nothing yet" / "Updates from your designer will land here." for a client whose Studio simultaneously shows two decisions "Overdue · Aug 22", an invoice "Due Sep 1" and a proposal "Review by Sep 8". Reproduced in dark mode.
why_it_matters: The one surface whose whole job is to say what changed says nothing changed, while four things are waiting two taps away.
proposal_seed: Write a notification_log row on proposal-sent, invoice-due and decision-created so the feed reflects the queue.

title: The one permission ask gives no reason
observation: Authorization is requested exactly once per install, immediately after the first successful design-request submission, with no pre-permission screen and no rationale copy anywhere in the app. A user who never submits a request is never asked. The Settings row "Notifications" writes a profile preference, not the OS grant.
why_it_matters: The most valuable return channel is spent in one unexplained system prompt at the one moment a user is least invested, and never offered to anyone else.
already_ruled: C28 (permission asked once, only after a design request, no pre-permission copy)
proposal_seed: Earn the prompt on the first real event — a decision or a shipment — with one sentence naming exactly what will be sent.

title: Push is live but fires for nothing money-shaped
observation: `apns-send` is complete and provisioned, with five callers repo-wide: three design-request SQL triggers, `fulfillment-notify` (operator-initiated, on the designer-sourced BOH rail), and `site-request-dispatch` (Field/trades). Zero callers touch invoices, proposals, decisions or direct orders; `invoice-reminders` and `proposal-nudge` are email and in-app rows only.
why_it_matters: The channel that could bring a client back for a proposal, an invoice or a delivery already exists and is wired to nothing a client cares about.
already_ruled: C26 (corrects C14: push send is real; none of it fires for money)
proposal_seed: Add one `invoke_edge_function('apns-send', …)` call site to the proposal-sent and invoice-due triggers.

title: Empty bell sells design help to a matched client
observation: The empty notifications state offers a "Get design help" button to an account with three projects, four proposals, an open $4,250 invoice and a named designer, Leah Hartwell.
why_it_matters: Being sold the thing you already bought is the clearest possible signal that the app does not know who it is talking to.
already_ruled: C17 (tier-narration empty copy is ratified) — the copy is ruled; showing the acquisition CTA at activeProject is the finding
july_status: U22 DELIVERED-CODE (empty states name trigger + conditional CTA) — the conditional is not conditioned on tier here
proposal_seed: Swap the CTA at activeProject to "Message Leah" or the oldest waiting item.

title: Two weeks away looks like one hour away
observation: A relaunch drops the signed-in client on a byte-identical "Today": no welcome-back, no unread marker, no last-visit timestamp, no activity feed. No last-seen timestamp exists for the feed, the story, the room or the saved list anywhere in the app; ContextMemoryStore records only a coarse activity kind and is off until the user turns it on. Two silent time-based changes are never explained: a matched request card disappears on day fifteen, and the Companion graduates to its calm state at fourteen days.
why_it_matters: An app that cannot say what happened while you were gone has no memory of you, and a home-furnishing project is measured in weeks, not sessions.
proposal_seed: Store a last-opened timestamp and render one dated "since you were here" line above the Next Move.

title: A returning guest is forgotten and called "home"
observation: A guest's session does not survive a relaunch: the taste portrait, the quiz progress and the session are discarded with no warning, and the screen that greets them reads "Welcome home". The saved piece and the coach-mark flags do survive, so the Companion insists "Style quiz — DISCOVER YOUR STYLE" while Profile simultaneously shows the "Warm Modern" badge and "48% MATCH".
why_it_matters: Someone who spent ten minutes answering questions is erased on the second launch and greeted as a returning resident — the exact opposite of both facts.
proposal_seed: Persist guest opt-in across launches and offer "claim your saves" at sign-in.

title: Status bar draws over scrolled content
observation: The fixed status bar draws over scrolled content with no inset reserved: "9:41" overprints "Awaiting payment" and "INV-2026-0142" on the invoice, "Invoices / 1 shared invoice" behind the Settings sheet, "Terms" on the proposal, and "Active projects" on the Studio list. At XXL the Dynamic Island pill itself occludes a proposal's title and its "Review by Sep 8" line, and a modal sheet's own "Close" and "Your design request" title.
why_it_matters: Dates and amounts are the words being covered, on the screens where money moves, and it gets worse at exactly the type size an older buyer uses.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B: touched screens recompose at accessibility text sizes)
proposal_seed: Reserve the top safe-area inset on every scroll container and sheet header.

title: Filter row clips "Storage" to "Stor" at XXL
observation: At Dynamic Type extra-extra-large the chip row "All / Seating / Tables / Lighting / Storage" overflows the screen width and "Storage" is clipped to "Stor" at the right edge, with no horizontal scroll affordance visible.
why_it_matters: A category silently disappears at the text size an older buyer actually reads at.
proposal_seed: Put the chip row in a horizontal ScrollView with a fade edge.

title: The orb covers the button it should help with
observation: The fixed circular Companion control sits on top of the primary action on multiple screens: it clips "Sign proposal" on the proposal detail, clips "Browse Picks for This Room" on the room, and at XXL the proposal's "Space Plan" body text runs directly under it and is cut off mid-sentence.
why_it_matters: The one control the app calls navigation obscures the two acts that matter most — signing and browsing — and gets worse at larger type.
already_ruled: C23 (Option B: "App content does not render beneath the active Companion shape") — the contract is ruled and violated here
proposal_seed: Apply the 120pt hearth inset to every scroll container, not just the home.

title: Room summary ignores dark mode
observation: The "YOUR SPACE / Here's what I see." summary step, with "Rescan" and "This Looks Right", renders on a cream background with near-black text while the rest of the app is in dark mode — the only screen observed to ignore the system/app appearance override.
why_it_matters: A full-brightness cream screen in the middle of a dark session is physically unpleasant, and it signals that the screen was built outside the design system.
already_ruled: C7 (dynamic dark mode via PatinaDesignKit tokens; camera/AR chrome is the only deliberate exception)
proposal_seed: Replace the hard-coded colours on the summary step with PatinaColors dynamic tokens.

title: The designer is named once, on the bill
observation: In the whole signed-in app the designer appears exactly once — "Aspen Loft Refresh · from Leah Hartwell" on the invoice detail, followed by an unattributed heading "A NOTE FROM YOUR DESIGNER". No photograph, no studio name, no bio, no credentials, no contact affordance — not on the home, the project, the proposal, or the decisions. Elsewhere the word "designer" appears only in empty states: "Updates from your designer will land here."
why_it_matters: The relationship is the product; a professional who appears only as a line above an amount owed is a vendor, not a designer.
proposal_seed: Put the designer's name, avatar and studio at the top of Today and on every document she authored.

title: The project screen shows the designer's to-do
observation: The client's project screen prints a stat labelled "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" — the raw `client_visibility_tier` column, shown to the client it governs — and a boxed line reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →", an instruction written for the designer, rendered to the homeowner, and not a button. The rest of the screen is three stats and an Invoices row, though the app successfully fetched project_phases and the client selections and rendered neither.
why_it_matters: Seeing the setting that controls how much you are allowed to see, next to your designer's homework, makes a paying client feel like a row in somebody's database.
proposal_seed: Delete both from the client build and render the phases the screen already fetched.

title: No way to say a word to the designer
observation: The entire messaging surface is a Studio block reading "Conversation  0" / "No project conversations yet." There is no compose, no thread list, no thread to open and no "message your designer" affordance anywhere in the signed-in app.
why_it_matters: A client with an overdue decision, an unpaid invoice and an expiring proposal cannot ask a single question inside the app, so every ambiguity becomes a phone call — the cost the designer was promised this would remove.
proposal_seed: Give every project a thread that exists from day one, with a composer on the empty state.

title: The signature sheet restates nothing
observation: The e-signature sheet shows "SIGN PROPOSAL", the project title, "Type your full name to e-sign. Signing confirms the scope and kicks off your project.", a "Full name" field, a disabled "Sign proposal" button and "Cancel". It restates no amount, no line items, no terms, no date and offers no agreement checkbox — while the terms one screen back read "Deposits are non-refundable once procurement begins. Custom items are final sale." and the total is $18,500.00.
why_it_matters: A legally binding signature collected without restating the sum or the non-refundable clause is both a trust failure and an enforceability risk.
already_ruled: C10 (the sign_proposal rail is ruled; the sheet's contents are not)
proposal_seed: Restate the total, the date and the two terms sentences above the signature field, with an explicit agreement tick.

title: An accepted proposal is filed as "SIGNED"
observation: The proposals list shows "SIGNED (1)" as a section header and "SIGNED" as the card status over "Sample accepted proposal / $100,000.00", for a proposal whose stored status is `accepted`; the seed contains zero signed proposals.
why_it_matters: Telling a client he signed a six-figure document he did not sign is a legally loaded error, and it is on the screen he would use to check.
proposal_seed: Label `accepted` as "Accepted" and reserve "Signed" for rows with a signature record.

title: "Your budget" is a bill, not a budget
observation: "BUDGET / Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" reports "$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING" and lists only Aspen Loft Refresh, for a client whose three projects total $725,000 on the projects list ($185,000 + $120,000 + $420,000). Formats mix on one card: "$4,250" above "$4,250.00".
why_it_matters: A screen headed "your budget across your projects" that omits 99.4% of the money is worse than no screen, because it will be believed.
proposal_seed: Either rename it "Billing" or include every project's budget and committed spend.

title: An $850 choice is one tap and irreversible
observation: "DECISION / Rug color - Natural vs Sand" presents two options, "Natural" badged "Recommended" and "Sand", both "$850", both with no image — a colour decision with no colour — under two identical black "Choose this" buttons. There is no way to ask a question, to defer, or to say neither, and nothing states the choice is final. Answering is three taps from a cold home; paying an invoice is five and signing a proposal is six.
why_it_matters: The shallowest, least-confirmed act in the app is the irreversible one that spends money, and it is presented without the one thing needed to decide it.
proposal_seed: Require the same confirm-and-sign step the app already uses, and show the option images the decision payload carries.

title: Payment failure is one red line under a live button
observation: When the checkout hand-off fails, the screen keeps "Pay $4,250.00" in full enabled styling and inserts one line of red body text below it — "Unable to start payment. Please try again." — which shoves "Pay securely by card or bank transfer" half off the bottom edge. There is no spinner, no retry affordance and no way to reach a human about a $4,250 payment that will not start. (The 503 behind it is the known local edge-runtime fault; the failure UX is the finding.)
why_it_matters: The worst moment in the money rail is handled with less care than an empty state, on the screen where the app is asking for four thousand dollars.
already_ruled: C27 (the 503 itself is a local-environment fault and is NOT claimed here)
july_status: U29/U30 DELIVERED-CODE (PatinaErrorState + one retry label) — this site renders a bespoke red line instead
proposal_seed: Render the canonical error state with a retry and a "contact your designer" link, and disable the button while in flight.

title: No Sign Out and no Delete Account anywhere
observation: Settings lists ACCOUNT ("Account", "Sign in on the web"), PREFERENCES ("Notifications", "Haptic Feedback", "Upload scans on cellular", "Appearance System"), PRIVACY & MEMORY and SUPPORT. There is no Sign Out and no Delete Account control anywhere in Profile or Settings, in guest or signed-in state; switching accounts during the walk required wiping the simulator keychain from the host. Guest Settings is byte-identical, offering an ACCOUNT section to someone with no account.
why_it_matters: An account you can create in the app and cannot leave or delete is both a trust failure for a cautious buyer and an App Store 5.1.1(v) exposure.
proposal_seed: Restore the Account screen so its existing Sign Out alert is reachable, and add account deletion.

title: "Account >" has a chevron and does nothing
observation: The Settings row "Account" draws a chevron and does not navigate — tapped dead-centre of its 338×44 frame with the screen unchanged, reproduced independently in the guest tier twice and the signed-in client tier once. `AccountView` exists in the codebase.
why_it_matters: A dead control on the account screen is the one place a cautious user checks first, and it is the app's own promise that nothing here is dead.
already_ruled: C5 (no dead controls)
july_status: U05 DELIVERED-CODE (all 7 named dead controls wired or removed) — this is a regression or a site not in that set
proposal_seed: Wire the row to AccountView, or delete the row.
